title: SDK Interop Cookbook: v1->v2 retries & streaming patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an SDK-focused interoperability cookbook that gives engineers a concise, example-driven migration path from v1 -> v2 across Python, TypeScript, and Go. The doc must: 1) explain semantic changes to streaming and how to map v1 patterns to v2 ergonomics, 2) document the unified retry middleware and default backoff/ idempotency guidance, 3) provide minimal reproducible examples for each language, 4) list deprecations and recommended shims, and 5) describe the changelog automation flow that surfaces breaking changes to customers. This ticket covers authoring, engineering review, and wiring the doc into the docs site + changelog automation playbook.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page cookbook PDF + markdown page exists under docs/sdk/migration with language sections for Python/TS/Go
Clear mapping table from v1 streaming callbacks/promises to v2 streaming iterator / async generator patterns
Unified retry middleware section with recommended defaults and code examples for integrating into existing apps
Deprecations table listing v1 APIs, replacement v2 API names, and suggested temporary shims
Changelog automation recipe that uses PR labels and a GH Action to produce structured changelog entries for release notes
Reviewer sign-off from SDK leads (Priya Patel, Diego Ramos) and Docs owner (Lina Martins)
Smoke-tested examples in our examples repo with CI passing for Python/TS/Go
Internal migration checklist added to migration playbook and linked from the Console rollout notes

implementation_notes: Streaming mapping decisions: provide 3 canonical patterns — 1) short-live responses -> use non-streaming v2 call, 2) continuous server-driven events -> v2 streaming async iterator with explicit cancellation, 3) chunked generation -> streaming iterator + incremental parse helpers

Retries: implement RetryPolicy with parameters {max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_strategy, retriable_statuses}. Default config: exponential backoff with full jitter, max_attempts=3. Document idempotency guidance per endpoint type.
Deprecations: schedule v1 streaming callback API for deprecation notice in 60 days, with shim to help 90% of customers migrate automatically for common cases.

Changelog automation: enforce structured PR titles like "[breaking] SDK: rename X->Y (#1234)" and parse labels in GH Action to produce entries. Store changelog entries as /artifacts/changelog/ sdk-2.0/structured.json for release automation.

Examples: put minimal runnable examples under examples/sdk-migration/{python,typescript,go} with Dockerfiles for local validation. Each example must include a test that verifies retry and streaming semantics in CI.
Telemetry: add lightweight telemetry events (opt-in) to track migration adoption: event names sdk.migration.start / sdk.migration.complete with variant (shim|native).
Backwards compatibility tradeoffs: shims can hide breaking behavior but may add maintenance surface and small latency penalty; recommend canary + canary traffic policy for production migration.
Docs UX: one-page cheat-sheet at top, then three language sections with copy-pasteable snippets and a regression checklist to run prior to switching production traffic.
